newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Intel busy as stock, sector fall.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Intel busy as stock, sector fall.

text.p: Intel Corp options were busy at the American Stock Exchange as the underlying shares led a decline in the sector on heavy volume.
Intel shares were down 2-3/4 at 139 on about 13.4 million shares by 1430 CDT/1930 GMT.

The technology-heavy Nasdaq composite index was down 7-1/2 points at about 1,242 after dropping to about 1,220. The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's semiconductor index lost 5.38, or 1.85 percent, to 283.63.
Traders said investors were playing both sides of Intel despite the drop in the stock.
Even so, sentiment appeared to favor further downside for both the sector and Intel's shares, traders said.
"The stock's down three and the rest of the computer stocks, with the exception of IBM (International Business Machines Corp), are down too," one options trader said.
"I think it was a sucker rally in the high techs to begin with," he added.
The Nasdaq composite fell from an all-time intraday high of about 1,400 on January 23 to 1,196 on April 3 before mounting a rebound.
Intel reached 165 on February 3 before dropping to 125-3/4 on March 24 and recovering.

One trader said he had been working some Intel options orders over the past couple of days and that overall, the trading pattern in the options did not suggest investors were leaning heavily toward the bullish or bearish side.
Trading in Intel options was led by the April 145 call, which had volume of 7,640 contracts by late trade. The April 140 call traded about 6,300.
On the put side, the Intel April 135 put traded a little more than 5,400 contracts and the April 140 put traded 4,965.
Several calls in the May series traded well over 2,000 contracts and volume was steady in the July and October series as well.
The Intel January 1998 130 put traded nearly 1,600 contracts and the January 1998 120 put traded nearly 1,100.
The January 1998 130 put had heavy open interest of more than 14,000 contracts. The option was up 1-1/2 at 11.
Among long-dated calls, the January 1998 150 was most active, with volume of nearly 400 contracts.
A few IBM options were active as the shares bucked the broader industry trend.

IBM rose 1-1/8 to 134-1/4 on more than two million shares. Most activity in the April options was on the call side, led by the April 105s, which traded 3,590 contracts. In the May series, however, turnover skewed to the put side, with the May 120, 125 and 130 puts each trading from 800 to 900 contracts.
Elsewhere in the group, Microsoft Corp, Qualcomm Inc and Cisco Systems Inc also had relatively active options.
